question.prompt:
A circle of radius \(5\) is inscribed in a rectangle as shown. The ratio of the length of the rectangle to its width is \(2:1.\) What is the area of the rectangle?

[Figure 1](figures/2012_AMC_10B_Q02_question_fig1.svg)

solutions.explanation:
Interpret “inscribed” as shown: the circle is tangent to the two long sides of the rectangle.

[Figure 1](figures/2012_AMC_10B_Q02_question_fig1.svg)

The radii perpendicular to these parallel sides form a diameter, so the width is \(2\cdot5=10\). The ratio \(2:1\) makes the length twice the width, or \(20\). Therefore the area is
\[
20\cdot10=\boxed{200}.
\]
There is a wording caveat. If “inscribed” requires tangency to all four sides, both rectangle dimensions must equal the diameter \(10\), producing a square rather than a \(2:1\) rectangle. Under the pictured two-side interpretation, the answer is \(\boxed{200}\), choice \(\boxed{\text{E}}\).
solutions.title: Diameter, ratio, and area
